title: Ashby API: Keys, Rate Limits, and Errors (2026 Guide)
summary: Ashby API access requires admin-created keys to read and write recruiting data.
body_markdown:
## Calling Ashby endpoints without code in Activepieces


For routine job syncs and new-application alerts, Activepieces lets you build the checklist's guardrails as a visual flow instead of a script you maintain. It offers unlimited flows on every plan, including free, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


Inside a flow, Ashby's limits still apply. A no-code step makes the same calls to the same endpoints, so it's throttled and rejected exactly as a script would be. Heavy custom syncs, such as backfilling your whole history, are better kept in code.


### Retries and failure handling in a workflow


In the screenshot, a webhook trigger feeds a single action step. The action's settings sit on the right: the connection, "Continue on Failure", "Auto Retry on Failure", and a test result with its output.


The example uses a different app's action, but an Ashby step sits in the same place. Retries and failure handling are switches on each step, and the test output shows what came back before you trust the flow.


Those two switches map to the guardrails. Auto retry covers transient errors, and "Continue on Failure" decides whether one bad record stops the run.


Leave it off for syncs where a silent gap would be worse than a loud stop. Add an alert step on the failure path, so errors reach you instead of sitting in a run log.


For routine reads, the HTTP step calls Ashby's list endpoints for jobs, applications and candidates exactly as the minimal request above does.


The same step covers any endpoint without a ready-made integration, and the core is MIT-licensed, so how a step behaves is something you can read in the source.


### Plans, keys and cost


I haven't confirmed which Ashby plans include API access, so ask your Ashby admin before building. If the key page is missing for your account, that's the answer.


Create the key in Ashby, grant only the permissions the flow needs, and store it in an Activepieces connection, not inside a step. A read-only alert flow should never hold write access.


On the Ultimate plan, or in a self-hosted enterprise setup, secret managers are listed in the feature set alongside SCIM, custom RBAC and audit logs, so the connection's secret can sit in your own vault rather than in Activepieces' database.


I have no confirmed per-unit price for Ashby, so I won't quote one.


On the Activepieces pricing page, checked 2026-10-23, the free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, which caps you at roughly 1,000 monthly executions regardless of complexity, so anything beyond occasional, light automation requires paid plans.


A flow that loops over every application therefore costs one credit per run, though Ashby's rate limits still apply to the loop.
